Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is named after our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), because his name is mentioned in it, and because the opening of the surah speaks of what was revealed to him and extols the status of those who believed in him.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Urging the fight against the disbelievers; God Most High's promise to the believers of reward for their deeds and the rectification of their affairs, and that their final destination is Paradise; an explanation of the duty of the believers to support the religion of God and repel the schemes of the enemies; and God's promise to them of victory over their enemies and the firmness of their feet in battle, provided they support the religion of God and honor His law.

• An explanation of the reality of disbelief and faith, by mentioning a number of the attributes of those who walk on both paths, and a comparison between the believers and the disbelievers in their goal, their condition and their end, and an explanation of the description of Paradise and its bliss, and of Hellfire and its punishment.

• A description of the stratagems of the hypocrites, the unveiling of their conspiracies and their character, and an indication of the connection between them and the Jews, and of their little contemplation of the Qur'an and their allegiance to the polytheists, and a threat that the Messenger (ﷺ) will be informed of their signs, and a warning to the Muslims not to be deceived by the hypocrisy of the hypocrites.

[The Tafsir]

Those who disbelieved, denying that God is the true God alone with no partner, and who barred people from His religion: God has nullified their deeds and rendered them void, and has made them wretched because of them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 2:

Those who believed in Allah, followed His law, and believed in the Book revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), which is the truth with no doubt in it from their Lord, He pardoned them, concealed from them the evil deeds they had committed, so He did not punish them for them, and He set right their affairs in this world and the Hereafter.

That misguidance and guidance have this cause: those who disbelieved followed Satan and obeyed him, while those who believed followed the Messenger (ﷺ) and what he brought of light and guidance. Thus Allah, exalted is He, has explained His treatment of the two groups, the people of disbelief and the people of faith, according to what each deserves. He, glorified is He, sets forth examples for people, and He joins to each group the likenesses and forms that befit it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 4–6:

When you meet, O believers, those who disbelieve on the battlefields, then strike [them] with the sword, and strike off their necks, until, when you have weakened them through much killing and broken their strength, then tighten the bonds on the captives: then either release them as a favor without ransom, or let them ransom themselves with wealth or something else, or take them as slaves or kill them. Continue in this until the war ends. That is the ruling mentioned regarding the trial of the believers with the disbelievers and the alternation of days between them. Had Allah willed, He would have granted victory to the believers over the disbelievers without fighting, but He made their punishment at your hands, so He legislated jihad, to test you through them and to make His religion victorious through you. As for those of the believers who were killed in the way of Allah, He will not nullify the reward of their deeds. He will guide them during their lives in this world to His obedience and His pleasure, and He will set right their condition, their affairs, and their reward in this world and the Hereafter, and He will admit them to Paradise, which He made known to them and described for them, and He guided them to do what He commanded them, among which is martyrdom in His way. Then, when they enter Paradise, He will make known to them their dwellings therein.

O you who have believed in God and His Messenger and acted according to His law: if you support the religion of God through jihad (striving in the way of God), ruling by His Book, carrying out His commands, and avoiding His prohibitions, God will support you against your enemies and make your feet firm in battle.

And as for those who disbelieve, destruction is theirs, and Allah has nullified the reward of their deeds. That is because they hated the Book of Allah that was sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), so they denied it, and so He nullified their deeds, because those deeds were in obedience to Satan.

And as for those who disbelieve, destruction is theirs, and Allah has nullified the reward of their deeds. That is because they hated the Book of Allah that was sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), so they denied it, and so He nullified their deeds, because those deeds were in obedience to Satan.

Have these disbelievers not traveled through the earth, taking warning from what befell the nations that denied before them of punishment? God destroyed their dwellings upon them, and the disbelievers will face the like of that outcome which befell those nations.

That which We have done to the two groups, the group of faith and the group of disbelief, is because Allah is the Protector and Helper of the believers, and because the disbelievers have no protector and no helper.

Allah will admit those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow, through their palaces and trees. This is an honour for them. As for those who disbelieve, their eating and enjoyment of this world is like the enjoyment of cattle, the livestock whose only concern is fodder and nothing else. The Fire of Hell is their dwelling and their abode.

And many of the people of towns who were mightier in strength than the people of your town, O Messenger, which is Makkah, which expelled you, We destroyed; and there was no helper for them to aid them against the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 14:

Is one who stands upon clear proof from his Lord, and knowledge of His oneness, like one to whom Satan has made his evil deeds appear good, and who follows what his own desires have called him to, of disobedience to Allah and worship of other than Him, without any proof or evidence? They are not equal.

The description of the Garden which Allah has promised to the God-fearing (al-muttaqun): in it are great rivers of water that does not change, and rivers of milk whose taste has not altered, and rivers of wine which those who drink it find delightful, and rivers of honey that has been purified of the impurities mixed with it. For these God-fearing people in this Garden there are all kinds of fruits, of every variety, and other things besides. And greater than all of that is the covering (of their sins) and the overlooking of their wrongdoings. Is then one who is in this Garden like one who abides in the Fire, never to leave it, and who is given to drink boiling water that has reached its utmost heat, so that it cuts their intestines to pieces?

Among these hypocrites are those who listen to you, O Prophet, without understanding, out of their own negligence and contempt. Then, when they leave your gathering, they say to those who have attended your gathering from among the people of knowledge of the Book of Allah, mockingly: "What did Muhammad just say?" They are those whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts, so they do not comprehend the truth and are not guided to it, and they follow their desires in disbelief and misguidance.
And those who were guided to follow the truth, Allah increased them in guidance. Through this, their faith grew strong, and He enabled them to attain piety and made it easy for them.

These deniers are only waiting for the Hour, which they were promised, to come upon them suddenly. Its signs have already appeared, yet they have not benefited from them. So how will they have any chance of remembering once the Hour has come upon them?

Know, O Prophet, that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin, and ask forgiveness for the believing men and the believing women. And Allah knows your movements while awake by day, and your resting places while asleep by night.

The believers say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?" But when a clear, decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is sickness (ﷺ-doubt and hypocrisy) looking at you, O Prophet, with the look of one who has fainted from fear of death. So woe to those in whose hearts is sickness; it would be better for them to obey Allah and to speak words that accord with the Sharia.

Then, when fighting becomes obligatory and the command of Allah to make it obligatory comes, those hypocrites dislike it. Had they been truthful to Allah in faith and in deed, it would have been better for them than disobedience and opposition.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 22:

Then it may be that if you turn away from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), you will disobey Allah on earth, disbelieve in Him, shed blood, and sever your ties of kinship.

Those are the ones whom Allah has removed from His mercy, so He has made them unable to hear what would benefit them or to see it, and so they have not understood the proofs of Allah, despite their abundance.

Will these hypocrites not reflect upon the admonitions of the Qur'an and ponder its proofs? Rather, these hearts are locked, and nothing of the meanings of this Qur'an reaches them, so they do not reflect upon Allah's admonitions and lessons.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 25:

Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them, and who reverted to disbelief in God after the truth had been made evident to them, Satan beautified their misdeeds for them and gave them false hope.

That granting of respite to them is so that they persist in disbelief, because they said to the Jews who hated what Allah had sent down: "We will obey you in some of the matter," which opposes the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger; and Allah, the Exalted, knows what these people conceal and what they keep secret. So let the Muslim beware of obeying anyone other than Allah in what contradicts the command of Allah, the Glorified, and the command of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 47, verse 27:

﴿So how will it be when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?﴾

That punishment is what they deserved and incurred, because they followed what angered God against them, namely obedience to Satan, and they disliked what would please Him with them, namely righteous deeds, including fighting the disbelievers after He had made it obligatory upon them. So God nullified the reward of their deeds, such as charity, maintaining the ties of kinship, and other things.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 47, verse 29:

Rather, did the hypocrites think that Allah will not bring out what is in their hearts of envy and malice toward Islam and its people? Yes indeed, Allah distinguishes the truthful from the liar.

Had We willed, O Prophet, We would have shown you their persons, and you would have recognized them by the distinct marks upon them. And you would surely know them by the manner of their speech, which indicates their intentions. Allah, exalted is He, is not hidden from Him the deeds of those who obey Him nor the deeds of those who disobey Him, and He will recompense each according to what he deserves.

We will surely test you, O believers, through fighting and striving against the enemies of Allah, until what He has known from eternity becomes manifest; so that We may distinguish among you those who strive and who are steadfast in fighting the enemies of Allah, and test your words and deeds, so that the truthful among you becomes evident from the liar.

Indeed, those who disbelieved, denying that Allah alone is the true God with no partner, and who barred people from His religion, and opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), fighting him after the proofs and signs had come to them that he is a prophet from Allah, will never harm the religion of Allah in the least; and He will nullify the reward of their deeds which they did in this world, because they did not intend thereby the Face of Allah, the Exalted.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law: obey Allah and obey the Messenger in what they command and what they forbid, and do not nullify the reward of your deeds through disbelief and sins.

Indeed, those who denied that Allah is the true deity, the one alone with no partner, and who barred people from His religion, and then died in that state, Allah will not forgive them. He will punish them as a retribution for their disbelief, and He will expose them before all the witnesses.

So do not falter, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, in fighting the polytheists, nor lose heart in combating them, nor call them to peace and reconciliation, for you are the dominant ones over them and the superior ones. Allah the Exalted is with you through His help and support. In this is a great good tidings of victory and triumph over the enemies. And Allah will not diminish the reward of your deeds.

This is the commentary of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex) on surah 47, verses 36–37:

"Indeed, the life of this world is merely play and delusion. And if you believe in Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, He will give you the reward of your deeds. And He does not ask you to give up all your wealth in zakat; rather, He asks you to give a part of it. If He were to ask you for your wealth and press you insistently and burden you, you would be stingy with it and withhold it from Him, and He would bring forth whatever resentment is in your hearts when you are asked for what you dislike to give away."

If He were to ask you for your wealth and press you insistently and burden you, you would be stingy with it and withhold it from Him, and He would bring forth whatever resentment is in your hearts when you are asked for what you dislike to give away."

Here you are, O believers, being called to spend in jihad against the enemies of Allah and in support of His religion. Among you are those who are stingy about spending in the way of Allah. Whoever is stingy is only being stingy toward himself, and Allah, exalted is He, is the One free of need from you, while you are the ones in need of Him. And if you turn away from faith in Allah and from obeying His command, He will destroy you and bring about a people other than you, who will not be like you in turning away from the command of Allah. Rather, they will obey Him and obey His Messenger, and they will strive in His way with their wealth and their selves.
